metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Northern Ireland agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Let's schedule the coordination meeting for September 7th, it's a good time before things get busy. What do you think, Hans?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: September 7th sounds like a decent choice, but have you considered September 5th? It gives us a bit more time to prepare before the busier part of the month kicks in. What's your thoughts on that?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: September 5th is okay, but I still think September 7th is better, it gives us a clearer picture of our progress. By the way, what's your stance on having the army rule, do you think it's always bad?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I'm not sure September 7th is the best for a progress update, but I can live with it. As for the army ruling, I think it's always a bad idea, people should have more control over their own governance, not some military force.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I disagree, having the army rule isn't necessarily bad, it can bring stability in certain situations. Let's stick with September 7th for the meeting, I think it's a good compromise.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I still don't think the army ruling is a good idea, it can lead to all sorts of problems. But, I suppose September 7th is settled then, let's just hope it works out for the project's sake.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I understand where you're coming from, Hans, and I think we're really not that far apart. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and I believe that's what matters here. The basic need to communicate is the same everywhere, and some values are just universal. So, let's not focus too much on our differences regarding the army ruling, but rather on our shared goal of making this project a success. We both know, at the end of the day, that it's about working together and finding common ground.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message: I... I understand what you're saying, but I still can't agree that having the army rule is a good idea. It's not about being different or the same, it's about what's right. And I think we should focus on the project now, September 7th is set, let's move forward with that.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.message: I'm not saying it's good or bad, just that it's not always bad, and that's my point. Anyway, since we've agreed on September 7th, let's prepare for the meeting and make sure everything goes smoothly. GOOD BYE!
